findings.text: dma_alloc_attrs provides coherent allocation with attribute control. It warns when coherent mask is missing and rejects compound page requests and confidential shared allocation requests. It honours forced unencrypted devices by adding an internal shared flag, tries per device coherent memory first, strips zone selection flags, then chooses direct allocation, IOMMU allocation, or driver ops allocation in order, emitting trace and debug hooks on outcomes.

dma_free_attrs releases coherent memory. It first tries release from per device coherent store, warns when called with interrupts disabled, traces the free, ignores null CPU addresses, records debug state, then dispatches to direct free, IOMMU free, or driver ops free according to allocation path predicates.

Managed allocation pairs device resource lifetime with coherent allocation. Allocation reserves a resource record, allocates coherent memory, fills size and handles and attributes, then attaches the record to the device. Release frees through the coherent free path. Matching compares virtual address for equality and warns on size or handle mismatch. Explicit managed free destroys the resource record and then frees.
dma_devres holds managed coherent allocation state as four fields in order: allocation size, CPU virtual address, DMA handle, and attribute flags.

dma_map_phys maps a physical range for DMA. It validates transfer direction, requires a DMA mask, rejects coherent only requests on non coherent devices, then selects direct mapping, architecture direct shortcut, IOMMU mapping, or driver backend mapping while handling memory mapped IO and confidential shared attributes distinctly, and finally runs sanitizer handling plus trace and debug hooks.

dma_unmap_phys reverses a physical range mapping. It validates direction, mirrors the direct and architecture direct checks used at map time, takes no action for confidential shared ranges beyond early return, otherwise delegates to IOMMU or driver backend unmapping, then emits trace and debug hooks.

Page based mapping converts page plus offset to a physical address and delegates to physical mapping. Mapping rejects memory mapped IO attributes and, under debug builds, rejects device memory pages. Unmapping ignores memory mapped IO requests and otherwise delegates to physical unmapping.

Scatter gather mapping validates direction, coherent requirements and DMA mask, then chooses direct, IOMMU, or driver backend mapping. Successful mappings run sanitizer, trace and debug hooks. Unexpected negative results are traced as errors and normalized to a generic IO failure, while recognized error codes propagate. One wrapper converts negative results to zero count and another stores the resulting count into the table and reports status.

Scatter gather unmapping validates direction, emits trace and debug hooks before backend work, then selects direct unmapping including an architecture direct shortcut, IOMMU unmapping, or driver backend unmapping.
Resource mapping marks physical mapping requests as memory mapped IO and delegates to physical map and unmap respectively, preserving direction and caller attributes.

Synchronization for single addresses and scatter lists validates direction, then dispatches to direct, IOMMU, or driver backend synchronization for the CPU facing and device facing variants, followed by trace and debug hooks.

dma_set_mask truncates the requested mask to DMA address width, fails when no mask storage exists or when the mask is unsupported, otherwise applies architecture handling, stores the mask, refreshes synchronization skip state, and reports success.

Backend selection prefers IOMMU presence, then driver support callback, then direct support. Direct mapping is a predicate over device, current mask and backend table. Synchronization skip state is derived from coherence when direct or IOMMU is used, forced skip when no sync callbacks exist, and cleared otherwise. An alternate build provides an empty synchronization setup.

Benchmark control arrives through an unlocked ioctl that copies parameters from user space, validates mode, thread count, duration, transmit delay, NUMA node, granule and direction, translates abstract direction into DMA direction, temporarily programs the device DMA mask from a bit width, runs the benchmark, restores the prior mask, propagates backend errors, and copies results back to user space.

Each benchmark worker prepares mode specific state, then loops until asked to stop: initialize data, time a map operation, fail out on map error, simulate transmit delay, time the corresponding unmap, convert both deltas to hundred nanosecond units, accumulate sums and squares of those units plus a loop count, and yield for scheduling. Preparation failure reports out of memory and unpreparation always runs on exit.

Benchmark orchestration allocates a thread handle array, holds a device reference, creates named workers on a requested node with optional NUMA binding and stops already created workers if creation fails, zeroes all accumulated statistics, holds task references and wakes workers, sleeps interruptibly for the requested seconds, stops all workers collecting their status, and on success derives average latencies and standard deviations from accumulated sums, squares and loop count when at least one iteration completed.

Benchmark mode selects an operations table containing prepare, unprepare, data initialization, map and unmap handlers. Single and scatter gather modes each have a dedicated table and selection is by indexing a mode sized array.

Device binding allocates zeroed benchmark state, registers a resource cleanup for debugfs removal, creates a single debugfs file with benchmark file operations where a second concurrent bind is intended to fail, and exposes identical probe logic through platform and PCI drivers registered at init and unregistered at exit with PCI registration rolled back if platform registration fails.

Benchmark statistics use atomic 64 bit accumulators for sums, squares and loop count, allowing lock free updates from many workers. Orchestration holds device and task references across worker lifetime and binding. Mapping helpers themselves show no explicit spinlock or mutex in these fragments.

Mapping paths treat invalid direction as a fatal bug check, missing DMA mask or coherent mask as warnings, mismatched managed free sizes as warnings, free in interrupt disabled context as warning, and allocation or mapping failures as null or error sentinel returns with tracing. Scatter gather error normalization prevents propagation of unexpected backend codes.

Benchmark ioctl rejects invalid user parameters, faulty user copies, mask programming failures, and worker errors, always restoring the original DMA mask after the run attempt. Probe reports allocation, resource action, and debugfs creation failures. Thread creation failure stops previously created threads before returning.

Benchmark user contract facts: debugfs file is named dma_map_benchmark with owner read write only; valid granule spans one to one thousand twenty four; NUMA node must be no node sentinel or a possible node below max nodes; transmit delay, thread count and seconds each have upper bound checks; mode must be below mode max; direction accepts bidirectional, device to memory, and memory to device abstract values.

Mapping, allocation, free, sync and scatter gather paths emit trace events and DMA API debug hooks on both success and failure, with unmap scatter gather tracing before backend dispatch and map scatter gather tracing only on positive entry counts.
The mapping translation unit defines trace point creation before including trace headers, enabling trace event instantiation in this object.
